question: How long does a Hacktoberfest Hack Day last and how many teams win the open-source AI prize?
answer_text: A Hacktoberfest Hack Day lasts 3 to 12 hours, with 4 to 6 hours being the recommended duration. The event is a one-day, in-person hackathon focused on building projects with open-source AI and open-weight models. 1 winning team is selected for the Best Open-Source AI Project prize at each Hack Day.

passages.text: Hacktoberfest Hack Days run for 3 to 12 hours, although four to six hours is ideal. Participants create and submit projects during the event for the Best Open-Source AI Project challenge. Use the MLH Standard Hackathon Rules as the default for your event: project-specific work happens during the Hack Day. If a different approach better suits your event, explain it clearly before project work begins. The challenge has one winning team, and every member receives a DEV Badge on their DEV account. Depending on availability and your event's onboarding instructions, MLH may also provide MLH+DEV branded swag bags for the winning team. The host selects the winner using the challenge guidance. Some Hacktoberfest Hack Day events will also receive a Hack Days partner prize category. These categories are assigned by the MLH Hacktoberfest team. See the partner challenge details.

Select Challenges in the “View and submit challenges for this event” banner. Confirm that the Best Open-Source AI Project challenge appears. If the MLH Hacktoberfest team assigned your event a Hack Days partner prize category, confirm that it appears too. If an expected challenge is missing, email hacktoberfest@mlh.io. Do not create a duplicate or add a partner category that MLH did not assign. You may add an optional local challenge through Edit Event → + Add Challenge. Keep it separate from the MLH challenges, which appear automatically. Any local prize is provided by the host unless your event onboarding says otherwise.
